worked_solution:
Since the given series is in the form ${\sum }_{n=1}^{N}a{r}^{n},$ it is a geometric series. 

To determine the sum, we use the formula for the sum ${S}_{N}$ of a geometric series.

$$
{S}_{N}={a}_{1}\frac{(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}
$$

In this case, $r=\frac{1}{4}$ and $N=4.$ We need to figure out the value of ${a}_{1}.$

The formula for the $n$th term of the series is

$$
{a}_{n}=10{(\frac{1}{4})}^{n},
$$

and therefore, we can calculate the first term ${a}_{1}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =10{(\frac{1}{4})}^{1} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

If we substitute ${a}_{1}=\frac{5}{2},r=\frac{1}{4}$ and $N=4$ into the formula for ${S}_{N}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=1}^{4}10{(\frac{1}{4})}^{n} & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{(1-{(\frac{1}{4})}^{4})}{(1-\frac{1}{4})} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{(1-\frac{1}{256})}{(\frac{3}{4})} \\  & =\frac{5}{2}\cdot \frac{(\frac{255}{256})}{(\frac{3}{4})} \\  & =\frac{425}{128}\end{aligned}
$$
